books.section: Topic 4.11 An Age of Reform, B. Debating the Future of Slavery in America

stimulus.text: In 1817, the American Colonization Society was founded to send free African Americans to Africa. Its supporters bought land in West Africa and founded the colony of Liberia. Between 1820 and the Civil War, about 12,000 African Americans went to Liberia. Most African Americans, free or enslaved, showed very little interest in leaving the United States to live in Africa.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.11, B. Debating the Future of Slavery in America: the American Colonization Society. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

options.text: all abolitionists supported together as one movement
options.misconception: Garrison and Douglass denounced colonization; abolitionists split over it.

rationales.A: Garrison called colonization racist and immoral, and Douglass attacked it too. Abolitionists divided sharply over the plan.
rationales.B: Some Southern whites supported colonization because it would rid the South of free Black people. The plan had Southern backers.
rationales.C: Some founders sympathized with Black Americans and hoped Liberia offered escape from racism; others saw Black people as inferior and wanted them gone. One plan, two motives.
rationales.D: The American Colonization Society was a private society, not a government bureau. Its money and ships were privately raised.
rationales.general:
1. List the supporters. Quakers and sympathizers stood beside slaveholders who wanted free Black people gone.
2. Ask why each joined. One side hoped for refuge, the other for removal.
3. Name the pattern. A single plan can carry opposite motives.
Background: About 7,000 of the settlers were enslaved people freed on condition that they leave the United States.
Remember: when strange allies share a plan, ask each side what it wants — the plan may mean two things at once.
